rubrics.criterion: The dormant explicit-event-loop adoption remnant is gone from both construction paths it affected: neither the connection constructor nor the pool constructor consults a disabled switch for adopting a caller-supplied loop anymore, and supported construction still resolves the event loop through the running-loop policy exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: This is the core loop-policy outcome of the modeled cleanup; it spans two components (driver connection and pool) whose constructors carried the same dormant option, so answering it requires confirming the retirement in both.

rubrics.criterion: The dormant notification-routing interface is completely retired: no import-time router definition, no router registry dictionary, and no routing decision inside the notification delivery loop remain, while supported LISTEN/NOTIFY delivery still forwards payloads through the connection's own notification queue with unchanged results.
rubrics.rationale: The notification consolidation is the second modeled cleanup; the remnant is a three-part structure (region, registry, branch inside the delivery loop) whose parts only disappear together, so the whole structure is one obligation.

rubrics.criterion: No stranded statements remain behind the unconditional failures that displaced them: the async-only paths that reject blocking operations no longer carry the superseded implementation after their raises, and the inactive-transaction commit no longer carries the old ancestor walk after its raise, with every one of those methods otherwise unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: The stranded-tail manifestations live in three different components and lifecycle phases (query cancellation, bulk copy entry, nested transaction commit); each is an independent location the solver must actually find rather than infer from one example.

rubrics.criterion: The dormant recycle-audit option is retired from the pool's idle-connection recycling decision, and the recycle decision still closes connections that idled past the configured interval exactly as before, without any warning or audit side effect in supported flows.
rubrics.rationale: The recycle lifecycle is the pool's own retirement in this case; the audit branch sits inside a live elif decision where its removal must not disturb the surrounding recycle timing.

rubrics.criterion: All three dormant SQLAlchemy-layer paths are retired: the undistilled raw-parameter forwarding in execute() parameter handling, the second-pass server-side default resolution in the dialect compiler, and the raw-positional row access in the result-row type are all gone, with supported parameter distillation, default prefetching, and mapping-style processed row access behaving identically.
rubrics.rationale: The sa layer carries three anatomically different dormant branches (module-level function arm, compiler early return, accessor precedence branch); confirming all three verifies the solver traced the integration layer as broadly as the driver layer.

rubrics.criterion: Retiring the guarded branches is accompanied by removing the module-level disabled switches those branches read: no module-level setting remains whose only purpose was enabling one of the removed paths, and no removed branch leaves its switch behind.
rubrics.rationale: Each dormant branch depends on its own switch constant; deleting branches while keeping their flags leaves the exact same residue the task asks to remove, so the switch retirement is a required companion change.

rubrics.criterion: Private helper functions that served only the removed paths are removed from their defining modules across the whole package: the loop-resolution helper in the shared loop-plumbing module, the pool's recycle-audit function, the execution layer's raw-arguments forwarder, and the dialect layer's second-pass defaults finder no longer exist anywhere.
rubrics.rationale: These helpers are defined outside the modules containing their callers, so passing core removal does not remove them; this rubric verifies the solver resolved names across module boundaries.

rubrics.criterion: Import statements were left consistent with the removal: no module imports a name from another module after the cleanup that nothing in the importing module uses, in particular the loop-plumbing name that only the removed constructor branches consumed.
rubrics.rationale: The dormant branches consumed imported aliases; a repair that removes branches and helpers but not their import lines leaves unused-import residue characteristic of an incomplete cleanup.

rubrics.criterion: A package-wide sweep over the whole aiopg package finds no surviving artifact of the retired paths: no switch constant, registry, router, helper, alias, guarded import-time region, or unreachable statement belonging to the modeled cleanups remains in any module of the driver layer or the sa layer.
rubrics.rationale: The case's central trap is that remnants are spread across seven modules in five different definition kinds; this rubric grades that the finished repair closed the whole set rather than the visible subset.

rubrics.criterion: The removal leaves the touched modules tidy: no empty registry or stub variable created by the cleanup remains declared, no guard condition remains whose body was deleted, and no module keeps a name binding whose definition site was removed.
rubrics.rationale: Mechanical deletions that leave guard heads, empty container declarations, or half-removed bindings are a concrete incomplete-repair signature specific to this injection's structure.

rubrics.criterion: The event-loop behavior of supported code regresses in no way: constructing connections, pools, or engines still works with the same arguments and results, explicit loop arguments remain unsupported exactly as before, and nothing in the library now requires or accepts a loop where it previously did not.
rubrics.rationale: The loop-policy code paths are the riskiest edit surface in this case; a plausible wrong repair activates the retired behavior instead of deleting it, or breaks running-loop resolution while deleting around it.

rubrics.criterion: Unsupported-use error behavior is unchanged: the async-only rejections still raise the same exception types with the same messages at the same inputs, and committing an inactive nested transaction still raises the library's invalid-request error rather than performing any commit or ancestor walk.
rubrics.rationale: Deleting statements behind raises (and beside them) makes it easy to disturb the surviving guard or the raise's message; this failure mode is established by this case's stranded-statement structure.

rubrics.criterion: Supported SQLAlchemy behavior regresses in no way: execute() still distills positional, keyword and iterable call sites into the same bound-parameter structures, compiled statements still resolve server-side defaults through the supported prefetch merge rather than any second pass, and key-based row fetches still apply result processors rather than raw values.
rubrics.rationale: The three sa dormant branches sit in the closest proximity to live processing paths; a wrong removal (dropping the live arm, flipping the precedence, removing the distillation) yields silently wrong query results, which is the concrete regression risk here.

rubrics.criterion: The public contract and the test suite are not reshaped: no public name, signature, default value, or exported symbol of the library changed, and no test file was modified to make the repair appear correct while the driver, pool, and sa modules were edited.
rubrics.rationale: The task's preservation boundary (public surface, no test edits) is explicit; verifying it requires comparing the edited modules' declarations against their pre-edit contract.

rubrics.criterion: Pool lifecycle behavior for supported configurations is unchanged: idle connections are still recycled at the configured interval with the same timing, no ResourceWarning or other audit side effect appears during recycling, and pool acquire/release semantics are identical.
rubrics.rationale: The recycle branch is embedded in the pool's release decision; a careless removal there can change which connections get closed (a silent pool-liveness regression) or leave a warning active, and this rubric targets exactly those risks.
